results.title: which leads to the rise of sequential recommendations. Sequential recommenders based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) (Tang and Wang, 2018), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) (Hidasi et al., 2016), and self-attention (Sun et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2019; Kang and McAuley, 2018; Zhou et al., 2020; Rajput et al., 2023) have become prevalent in the era of deep learning. Notably, leveraging a T5-like backbone, Rajput et al. 2023 formalize recommendation as generative retrieval, i.e., autoregressively decode the identifiers of the target items, and achieve the current SOTA. While structurally resembling LLMs, it lacks their pre-training knowledge and the accompanying natural language reasoning potential. Our proposed approach adopts self-attention for sequential recommendation, specifically harnessing LLMs as backbones. We compare against various baselines from all the classes discussed above.

item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports learning substitute/complement relationships when additional supervision exists. [SCRM (2023/2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.14957) constructs separate relationship graphs from click and purchase sequences, then applies denoising and relationship constraints; its experiments report component ablations. Those behavior distinctions are unavailable here. [KGSCL (2025)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S089360802500070X) uses Amazon metadata’s explicit substitute/complement relationships to guide substitution and insertion augmentations. Those relationship fields also exceed the supplied data contract. Neither establishes that titles/descriptions plus a single interaction stream reliably identify complements.\n\nText-based sequential recommendation results require care: [Recformer (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13731) combines language/recommendation pretraining; its reported no-pretraining ablation performs substantially worse. [WhitenRec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.10602) explicitly depends on pretrained text embeddings. These results therefore do not establish gains under the train-from-scratch restriction. A feasible experimental hypothesis is a small randomly initialized token-pooling encoder over supplied titles/descriptions, fused with SASRec ID embeddings and trained using observed next-item supervision. Compare ID-only, text-only, fused, and shuffled-text controls using the fixed macro validation HR@10; separately inspect sparse-item behavior. Treat learned directional transitions as predictive associations, not verified complement labels. Text overlap can share statistical strength, but these sources provide no basis for inferring ownership, compatibility, or an unmet need from similarity alone."}
